_metadata.independence: I read only the brief and x19-re-input.json, opened no other repository file, and used no web or paid API.

hints.reason: ANGEL via the familiar image of angels playing harps; SEAL via the harp seal, named for its harp-shaped back marking; two unrelated worlds meet cleanly.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pairing; a genuine 'oh, nice' double route.

hints.reason: BABY via the folklore stork that delivers babies; NEST via the stork's famous big rooftop nests, a bird-plus-property link in the PENGUIN mould, slightly softer than the baby side.

pairs.pair_note: Baby side is instant; nest side is fair once you think 'bird'.

hints.reason: BASKETBALL via the dunk itself; JAM via its basketball-slang sense (a jam is a dunk), which pulls JAM away from its fruit sense for a small aha.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but clean; the synonym note is not a problem here.

hints.reason: BEAT via "Beat It"; GLOVE via Michael Jackson's iconic single sequined glove; both are signature Jackson facts.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; two of the most recognizable Jackson details.

hints.reason: SWEET via the instantly familiar phrase "sweet sixteen"; BIRTHDAY because a sweet sixteen is a sixteenth-birthday celebration; clear and tidy.
hints.fix: SWEET line: A sixteenth birthday is nicknamed a "sweet sixteen."

pairs.pair_note: Easy phrase-join that genuinely clicks; the SWEET line is circular and is worth rewording.

hints.reason: BOLT via "lightning bolt"; FAST via "lightning fast"; both phrases are instantly familiar, with a bonus Usain Bolt echo.

pairs.pair_note: Solid, familiar phrase-join.

hints.reason: BOX via the famous boxing kangaroo; GLOVE via the classic image of a kangaroo in boxing gloves; the glove side leans on that cartoon image but it is iconic (BOXING would be more direct but contains BOX, so KANGAROO is the right choice).

pairs.pair_note: Works through one iconic image; note KANGAROO is also a target elsewhere in this batch (p_kangaroo__punch), which the builder should keep off the same board.

hints.reason: BUBBLE via "bubble wrap"; MUMMY via mummies being wrapped in linen; the packing-material/mummy contrast is a fun picture.

pairs.pair_note: Strong and playful.

hints.reason: BUTTON and EYE both via Coraline's famous button eyes, the defining image of the film and its poster.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; one iconic image covers both words.

hints.reason: CEREAL via Cap'n Crunch cereal; CAP via "Cap'n" (cap/cap'n as short for captain), a slight sound stretch but the brand name clicks fast once CAP is on the board.
hints.fix: CAP line: "Cap" is a nickname for a captain, like Cap'n in Cap'n Crunch.

pairs.pair_note: Fair brand clue; the CAP line should connect the hint to CAP rather than just define Cap'n.

hints.reason: CARROT via the classic carrot nose; STICK via the classic stick arms; both are core snowman details.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent and wholesome; avoids the obvious carrot-and-stick idiom route.

hints.reason: CHAIR via "deck chair"; TITANIC via the ship's decks and the idiom "rearranging the deck chairs on the Titanic"; the idiom gives a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the idiom lifts this above a plain phrase-join.

hints.reason: CHRISTMAS via Santa himself; FATHER via Father Christmas, the British name for Santa that most U.S. players know from films and books.

pairs.pair_note: Fair and easy; british_only is a familiarity note only, Father Christmas is widely known in the U.S.

hints.reason: COAT via the trench coat; WAR via trench warfare; the explanation adds the true link that the coat is named for WWI trenches.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the shared WWI origin turns a phrase-join into a satisfying fact.

hints.reason: COTTON via Eli Whitney's cotton gin (standard U.S. school history); LOVE via Whitney Houston's "I Will Always Love You"; two different Whitneys is a clever twist, though the LOVE side rests on one song title.

pairs.pair_note: Clever two-person route; love side is softer but the song is iconic enough.

hints.reason: DEER via a buck being a male deer; PASS via "pass the buck"; a classic clean double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent double meaning.

hints.reason: DOG and DOWN both via the downward dog pose, one of the best-known yoga poses.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair; one pose covers both words.

hints.reason: DWARF via the Seven Dwarfs singing "Heigh-Ho"; WORK via its famous line "off to work we go"; instantly recognizable.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent and fun to solve.

hints.reason: FACE via "facepalm"; TREE via "palm tree"; both compounds are everyday words and the gesture/tree contrast is pleasant.

pairs.pair_note: Clean phrase-join.

hints.reason: FAN via stadium fans doing "the wave"; SURFING via ocean waves; a crisp double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent double meaning.

hints.reason: FIRST and LADY via FLOTUS, the well-known acronym for First Lady of the United States; a quick decode with a small payoff.

pairs.pair_note: Easy decode; the acronym is familiar from news coverage.

hints.reason: FOUNTAIN via tossing coins into fountains like the Trevi; WELL via coins in a wishing well; a clear shared custom.

pairs.pair_note: Fair and easy; WISH is an equally good alternative, not clearly better.

hints.reason: GAME via the party game Twister; TONGUE via "tongue twister"; both are instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Clean and familiar.

hints.reason: GOD and WAR both via the God of War video game title, which works for gamers but Kratos's name is fandom knowledge many general players lack; ARES (or MARS), the god of war, reaches both words for everyone.

pairs.pair_note: Facts are correct, but the hint leans on gaming fandom when a mythology hint is broader and cleaner.

hints.reason: HAMMER via sledge/sledgehammer; SISTER via the band Sister Sledge, whose song "We Are Family" is far better known than the group's name, so the sister side needs explanation for many players.

pairs.pair_note: Facts are fine; the band-name phrase-join is not instantly familiar.

hints.reason: HOCKEY via the hockey goalie; MASK via the goalie mask; direct and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and solid; JASON (Friday the 13th's hockey mask) would be a fun alternative, not clearly better.

hints.reason: HOUSE via Dobby the house-elf; SOCK via the sock that frees him; both are signature Harry Potter facts.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; mainstream reference with a satisfying click.

hints.reason: JAM via "paper jam"; PRINTER via printer paper and its notorious jams; relatable and instantly clear.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, relatable; note JAM is a target in another pair too (p_basketball__jam).

hints.reason: KANGAROO via the famous boxing kangaroo; PUNCH via boxing being the sport of punching; clear on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: Fair and easy; keep away from the BOX/GLOVE pair whose hint is KANGAROO.

hints.reason: LEGO via LEGO bricks; SHOT via the basketball slang "brick" for a badly missed shot; a satisfying toy/sports double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong double meaning; basketball slang is widely known in the U.S.

hints.reason: MATCH via "match point"; TENNIS only via points being its scoring unit, so the clue mostly restates the already obvious tennis match link with little payoff.

pairs.pair_note: Correct but flat; MATCH and TENNIS already pair on their own, so the hint adds little. Unsure whether the owner would still accept it as an easy clue.

hints.reason: TOOTH via tooth enamel; NAIL via nail enamel, a real and fairly well-known name for nail polish; the nail side is softer but true and gives a small aha.

pairs.pair_note: Fair; the nail side relies on the cosmetic term, which many players know.

hints.reason: NOODLE and SOUP both via ramen being a noodle soup; easy and direct.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, clear clue.

hints.reason: PALM via Palm Sunday, the Sunday before Easter; SUNDAY via Easter Sunday; a clean calendar link.

pairs.pair_note: Fair and familiar.

hints.reason: PHONE via "cell phone"; ROOM via a cell as a small room, as in a prison cell; a fair double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Solid double meaning.

hints.reason: PUPPET via the Muppets being Jim Henson's puppets; SHOW via The Muppet Show; easy, and the near-rhyme with PUPPET is a fair nudge rather than containment.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and familiar.

hints.reason: ROME via the Roman Empire; STATE via New York's Empire State nickname; two very different empires is a nice twist.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; note EMPIRE is also the hint for p_star-wars__strike.

hints.reason: SEAL via the elephant seal, named for the male's trunk-like nose; TRUNK via the elephant's trunk; the shared nose makes it click.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; the trunk detail ties both sides together.

hints.reason: WITCH via Macbeth's famous three witches; SISTER via their name "the Weird Sisters," which many players remember only once told, so one side is weak.

pairs.pair_note: Facts are correct; the sister side depends on a school-English detail, so it sits on the line.

hints.reason: STAR WARS via the Galactic Empire; STRIKE via The Empire Strikes Back; one beloved title covers both.
hints.fix: STRIKE line: The Empire Strikes Back is the title of the 1980 Star Wars sequel.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; the STRIKE line is a little awkward and could be cleaner.

hints.reason: THIN via "thin as a rail"; TRAIN via trains running on rails; both familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Clean and fair.

hints.reason: WINTER via Narnia's "always winter and never Christmas"; WITCH via the White Witch of The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe; both central to the story.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; mainstream classic with both words at its heart.
